This suit is filed for partition and separate possession of 1/6th share each of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit schedule 'A' & 'B' properties in terms of the Will dated 29.10.1997, and for costs and such other reliefs.
2. The brief facts of the case as per the plaint are :

The plaintiffs and defendants are the children of B. Ramalingappa and Smt M.
Kamakka.
The mother - Smt M. Kamakka has died in the year 1982.
The father had acquired the various properties during his lifetime.
The father of the plaintiffs and defendants had lost his parents at an early age and B. Ramalingappa - father of the plaintiffs and defendants was looked after Smt Hanumakka, who had no issues.
He succeeded the properties of the said Smt Hanumakka.
The properties at Subedar Chatram Road, Annamma Temple Extension, Bengaluru, were acquired by the father of the plaintiffs.

He acquired his property at Nagadevanahalli, Kengeri Hobli,
Bengaluru South Taluk, to the extent of 8 acres of land.
B. Ramalingappa provided good education to the children and the defendant No.1 joined the service in Commercial Tax O.S.No.6422/2006 Department.
The defendant No.2 was employed in Bharath Electronics Limited and the defendant No.3 joined the service in ITC Company at Bengaluru.
B. Ramalingappa had executed a Will dated 20.06.1983, and it is registered with the Office of the SubRegistrar at Gandhinagar, Bengaluru.
A codicil was made in the year 1983.

Later in the year 1997, B. Ramalingappa cancelled the Will and executed another Will on 29.10.1997, and in the said Will, B. Ramalingappa has stated that, on 20.06.1983 when he was ill and he was hospitalized got written the Will dated 20.06.1983.
The defendants No.1 to 3 have got written the said Will and they did not look properly.
B. Ramalingappa had received a compensation due to the land acquisition and same was also distributed to the plaintiffs and defendants.

sentences.text: B. Ramalingappa has died on 25.12.1997 and the said Will dated 29.10.1997, is enforceable.
The plaintiff No.1 has been allotted schedule 'A' property.
The plaintiff No.2 is allotted the schedule 'B' property.
The BBMP also has got mutated the names as per the Will.

In respect of the properties situated at Annamma Temple Extension,
Bengaluru, it is kept pending.
Both plaintiffs have been given right to construct the 2 nd floor in the terrace area over and above existing 1st floor of the buildings concerned.
The defendants did not allow the Corporation Bank, S.C. Road Branch, Bengaluru, to make payments under the Fixed Deposits, as there was no specific reference in the said Will dated 29.10.1997.
So, the succession certificate is obtained under P & SC No.73/1999.

Then the defendants No.1 to 3 filed suits in O.S.No.5088/2000,
O.S.No.5101/2000 & O.S.No.5184/2000 , for recovery of the amount and the said suits are pending.
The suit in O.S.No.6037/1999 is also filed for injunction.
But the plaint has been rejected.
The defendants No.2 & 3 filed similar suits in O.S.No.6039/1999 & O.S.No.6035/1999, and they are pending before the respective Courts.

The defendants No.1 to 3 have been collecting the rents out of the properties bearing Nos.461, 462 & 463, situated in Old Poor House Road and the property bearing No.100 situated in Commercial Street at Bengaluru.
The defendants No.1 to 3 are amassing wealth, So, when such being the case, the plaintiffs requested for effecting the partition in accordance with the Will dated 29.10.1997.
But the defendants did not comply.
In the month of O.S.No.6422/2006 May 2006, the property situated at Krishnappa Galli, Cottonpet, Bengaluru, the defendants have made developments.

It was also revealed that, the defendant No.2 and his wife along with children have executed a registered sale deed and it was also revealed that, the khatha has also been changed in the name of M.R. Krishnasa.
This itself shows the dishonesty on the part of the defendants.
The defendants are asserting the rights based on the Will dated 20.06.1983.
So, the defendants have tried to defeat the rights of the plaintiffs.

The cause of action for the suit arose on the death of B.
Ramalingappa and on subsequent dates of filing the petitions and during the month of May 2006, when the property has been sold by the defendants to the third persons.
Hence, it is prayed to decree the suit.
3. On issuance of suit summons, the defendant No.1 has appeared and filed detailed written statement contending that, the averments of the plaint are all false.
The suit is not maintainable.

B.
Ramalingappa is the propositor married Smt M. Kamakka and begotten the plaintiffs and defendants No.1 to 4.
With the able assistance of defendants No.1 to 3, B. Ramalingappa purchased the immovable properties.
O.S.No.6422/2006 B. Ramalingappa executed a registered Will on 20.06.1983, and all the properties were bequeathed.
The plaintiffs were given gold articles worth Rs.1.5 lakhs.

The defendant No.1 is in possession of the property, which is bequeathed under the Will of 1983, and there is no question of bequeathing the terrace or upper floor of the said property in favour of any other person.
The Will of 1983 is already acted upon.

So, considering the Will dated 29.10.1997, does Smt B.R. Anasuya vs Sri B.R. Aulappa on 31 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34542603/

The contention that, B. Ramalingappa lost his parents during his childhood and he was looked by Smt Hanumakka and thereafter, B. Ramalingappa succeeded the properties of Smt Hanumakka also denied.
It is also denied as to the acquisition of the properties by B. Ramalingappa in respect of the properties situated at Annamma Temple Extension and Nagadevanahalli, Bengaluru.
The defendants No.1 to 3 have acquired their possession out of their own individual efforts.

It is averred by the defendant No.1 that, B. Ramalingappa had executed a Will dated 20.06.1983, and thereafter,
a codicil was also written.

The averment that, B. Ramalingappa has distributed Rs.1,00,000/
O.S.No.6422/2006 each to the plaintiffs and defendants, is all denied.
It is also denied that, the defendants No.1 to 3 have got written the Will when B. Ramalingappa was not keeping good health.
It is denied that, the defendants No.1 to 3 did not look after B. Ramalingappa properly.
It is denied as to the averments in para10 of the plaint that as per the Will dated 25.12.1997, the BBMP has entered the names of the plaintiffs.
It is denied that, the defendants did not allow to take Fixed Deposits amount and also other properties.
It is denied that, the defendants have filed false suits in the year 2000.
It is denied that the defendant No.1 filed a false suit in O.S.No.6037/1999.
It is also denied that, the suits in O.S.No.6035/1999 and O.S.No.6039/1999 were false suits.
The suit in O.S.No.6035/1999 has been decreed on 01.01.2008.
It is denied that, the defendants are letting the properties on rent and making huge income.
It is denied that, the plaintiffs have sought for partition and the defendants have denied to give the share as per Will dated 29.10.1997.
It is denied that, the defendant No.1 has sold the property, by which the plaintiffs herein have filed the suit.
The plaintiffs are very much aware that the Will dated 20.06.1983, is already acted upon and filed a false suit for O.S.No.6422/2006 claiming the property.
Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the suit with exemplary costs.
4. The defendant No.2 has appeared and filed separate written statement and has taken up the same contentions of the defendant No.1.
Further he has added that the suit is filed to make wrongful gain by the plaintiffs.
The Will dated 20.06.1983 was written by B. Ramalingappa when he was maintaining good health and sound state of mind at the age of 66.
B. Ramalingappa took signatures of the family members as witnesses to avoid misunderstanding and confusion.
All the three daughters of B. Ramalingappa have been given several crores of properties along with gold and cash.
In pursuance of the Will of 1983 as soon B. Ramalingappa died in the year 1997, the properties have been allotted and the Will of 1983 is acted upon.
The plaintiffs nor defendant No.4 have raised any objection in respect of the Will of 1983.
So, having no other way, the this defendant has filed the suit in O.S.No.6039/1999.
The defendants No.1 to 3 have looked after B. Ramalingappa properly.

Hence,
it is prayed to dismiss the suit with exemplary costs.

The defendant No.3 also denied the plaint averments in the line of defendants No.1 & 2.
It is contended that, the plaintiffs have filed P & SC and had taken 1/6th share amount of fixed deposits from the bank.
It is admitted as to the rejection of suit in O.S.No.6037/1999.
It is also admitted as to filing of two suits in O.S.No.6035/1999 and O.S.No.6039/1999.
It is denied that, the defendants No.1 to 3 are receiving the rent and making huge amount.

It is denied that the defendants are excluding the Smt B.R. Anasuya vs Sri B.R. Aulappa on 31 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34542603/

sentences.text: It is denied that the defendant No.1 sold the property.
The basis for the plaintiffs to seek partition is the Will dated 29.10.1997.
The Will is concocted one.
B. Ramalingappa was bedridden, by the time the the alleged Will of 1997 was written.
The health of B. Ramalingappa was so serious and he lost his memory during 1997.
He was not in a position to understand what has been written in the Will.
The Will of 1983 was executed in good health and sound mind.
So, the Will of 1983 has been acted upon.

The plaintiffs by creating the documents have taken the money deposited by B.
Ramalingappa in the Corporation Bank.
So, the suit in O.S.No.5101/2000 was filed.

As on this day,
the plaintiffs and defendants are in possession of the property according to the Will executed in 1983.
Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the suit with exemplary costs.

6. The legal representatives of the defendant No.3 have also appeared and filed an additional written statement and contended that, the property bearing Sy.No.21 of Nagadevanahalli village has been already acquired and the proceedings in LAC No.326/1989 have been completed and there is no dispute.
The Will of 1983 has been acted upon and all the members of the family are in possession of respective properties as absolute owners.

B. Ramalingappa has died in the month of December,
1997.
The Will put forth by the plaintiff is 29.10.1997.
Though the Will of 1997 makes reference to the Will dated 20.06.1983, there is no any reference made in respect of codicil dated 24.06.1983.
Since the Will of 1983 is acted upon, the question of considering the Will dated 29.10.1997 is a forged and fabricated and there is no signature of B. Ramalingappa nor O.S.No.6422/2006 LTM.
The witnesses so shown are no way related to B. Ramalingappa.

It is also mentioned that B.
Ramalingappa was a chronic alcoholic.
Further the plaintiffs have taken the share according to the Will of 1983.
In the year 1994, B. Ramalingappa had fall and suffered head injuries.

Since 1994, B.
Ramalingappa was not in good health and state of mind, he has suffered paralytic stroke.
So, the question of executing the Will dated 29.10.1997, does not arise.
The legal representatives of defendant No.3 have made allegations that the defendant No.4's handwriting is seen in the Will dated 29.10.1997.
The averments made in the Will are such that, it cannot be act upon.
So, the question of considering the Will of 1997, does not arise.
The plaintiffs also have taken the share of their properties under the Will dated 20.06.1983.
So, the question of seeking 1/6th share does not arise.
Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the suit with exemplary costs.
7. The defendant No.5 being the purchaser of the property, has filed separate written statement and contended that the frame of the suit itself is improper.
The plaintiffs on one hand claim rights under the Will and wards claim partition under the O.S.No.6422/2006 same Will.
There is no cause of action for filing the suit so also Will is an hindrance of succession.
So, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
The defendant No.5 is the purchaser of the property.
The averments in para No.1 to 8 of the plaint does not pertain to the defendant No.5.
In respect of para No.9 of the plaint, the averments have been denied by defendant No.5.
The property has been purchased by defendant No.5 since the properties were in the name of seller and the Will so executed in the year 1997, would not operate against the present defendant No.5.

sentences.text: 9 12. Issue No.1:
As per the plaint averments, it is averred that the father had acquired various immovable properties and also made deposits.
It was narrated that, Late B. Ramalingappa was a Contractor and has quired the properties.
13. It is also put forth in para5 of the plaint that, B. Ramalingappa succeeded the properties of Smt Hanumakka, who had no issues and the said Smt Hanumakka was aunty of B. Ramalingappa.

In para6 of the plaint, the plaintiffs have contended that the immovable properties bearing No.19 &
20 near Annamma Temple Extension, Bengaluru, are the self acquired properties.
The properties bearing Sy.Nos.21 & 22 of Nagadevanahalli, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South taluk, are the self acquired properties.
In the written statement the defendants had taken up a contention that, the defendants No.1 to 3 also O.S.No.6422/2006 have contributed for purchase of the property.
It is denied that, the father - B. Ramalingam had succeeded the properties of Smt Hanumakka.
The defendant No.1 has denied the acquisition of the property by the vendor.
14. In the crossexamination of PW.1, a suggestion is made with the properties situated at Cottonpet, Jumma Masjid Road and Commercial Street, have been acquired by B. Ramalingappa from Smt Hanumakka.
The suggestion is admitted by PW.1.
Further it is also suggested that, the said Smt Hanumakka is the elder sister of his father's mother - Smt Hanumakka.
It is also admitted that, Smt Hanumakka bequeathed the said property by Will in favour of B. Ramalingappa.
So, by suggestion the defendants are admitting that the properties at Jumma Masjid Road so also on Commercial Street are bequeathed in favour of father of plaintiffs.
So, the properties before this Court consist of selfacquired properties so also the separate properties acquired through Will.
15. In this case both the parties have not denied the relationship to each other and they are contending in regard to the Will dated 29.10.1997.
In this case there was a Will dated 20.06.1983 executed by father and again present plaintiffs herein are claiming share based on the Will dated 29.10.1997.
So, the question of properties whether selfacquired properties or separate properties would not gain much importance to decide the case.
However, since the plaintiff has contended that all the properties in the name of father were self acquired properties.
But it revealed even as per the plaint averments that some of the properties are the separate properties.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 'Partly in the affirmative'.
17. Issue No.2, 3, 5, 6 and Addl. Issue No.1: Since these issues are interrelated, they are hereby discussed together to arrive at a conclusion.
18.
In this case the plaintiffs have sought their share based on the Will dated 29.10.1997 executed by the father - B. Ramalingappa.

The defendants are contending that, the father had executed a Will in the year 1983, and as per the Will dated 20.06.1983, the shares have been already taken by the children of B. Ramalingappa and they are already in possession and enjoyment of the properties.

So,
the question of considering the O.S.No.6422/2006 Will dated 29.10.1997, does not arise.

The plaintiffs are contending that, their father - B. Ramalingappa has executed the earlier Will dated Smt B.R. Anasuya vs Sri B.R. Aulappa on 31 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34542603/
10 20.06.1983.

sentences.text: Then a fresh Will has been executed on 29.10.1997.
By the said Will, B. Ramalingappa has bequeathed the schedule 'A' property in favour of plaintiff No.1 and schedule 'B' property in favour of plaintiff No.2.
The defendants are contending that, the Will dated 20.06.1983 is already acted upon.
So, the question of considering the Will dated 29.10.1997, does not arise.
So, in this regard, the Court has to assess the evidence of the parties.
First and foremost, the plaintiffs have to produce the original Will to prove the Will as well as signature on the Will dated 29.10.1997.

But in this case the plaintiffs did not care to produce the Will dated 29.10.1997 and got marked only a certified copy of the Will dated 29.10.1997.
19.
The plaintiffs have approached the Court seeking their share as per Will dated 29.10.1997.
So, it is the burden on the plaintiffs to produce the original Will and prove the Will as per law by adducing the evidence of attesting witness.
In this case O.S.No.6422/2006 the Will dated 29.10.1997 has not seen the light of the day till this day.
20. During the crossexamination PW.1 has stated that the Will is not with her.
In that case she has to call upon the person who has got Will and produce the same.
She has to make out who are the attesting witnesses to the said Will and called them for giving evidence before the Court.

No effort has been made out by the plaintiff to prove the Will dated 29.10.1997.
21.

The learned Counsel for defendants herein has drawn the attention of the Court to the cross examination of PW.1 that, at page No.5 PW.1 has clearly admitted that, "It is true that my father has executed a Will on 20.06.1983 and it is registered Will.
It is true that my father executed codicil on 24.06.1983".
So, the plaintiff is very much aware of the Will dated 20.06.1983 and also codicil made on 24.06.1983.
A strong contention of the defendant is that, the said Will dated 20.06.1983 has been acted upon.
Subsequently, the plaintiffs herein to make unlawful gain have put forth a concocted Will of 1997 that too after the death of the father about 9 years later.

So, the learned Counsel for the defendant has contended that, this inordinate delay to claim the O.S.No.6422/2006 share on the basis of the Will of 1997 itself shows that the Will so executed on 29.10.1997, is nothing but a concoction to make unlawful gain.

22. The learned Counsel for defendant also has drawn the attention of the Court to the cross examination to prove that the Will of 1983 has already been acted upon and shares as per Will of 1983, are already taken and respective brother or sister in the possession of the said property.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The father had acquired the various properties during his lifetime.
The father of the plaintiffs and defendants had lost his parents at an early age and B. Ramalingappa - father of the plaintiffs and defendants was looked after Smt Hanumakka, who had no issues.
He succeeded the properties of the said Smt Hanumakka.
B. Ramalingappa provided good education to the children and the defendant No.1 joined the service in Commercial Tax O.S.No.6422/2006 Department.
The defendant No.2 was employed in Bharath Electronics Limited and the defendant No.3 joined the service in ITC Company at Bengaluru.
B. Ramalingappa had executed a Will dated 20.06.1983, and it is registered with the Office of the SubRegistrar at Gandhinagar, Bengaluru.
A codicil was made in the year 1983.
Later in the year 1997, B. Ramalingappa cancelled the Will and executed another Will on 29.10.1997, and in the said Will, B. Ramalingappa has stated that, on 20.06.1983 when he was ill and he was hospitalized got written the Will dated 20.06.1983.
The defendants did not allow the Corporation Bank, S.C. Road Branch, Bengaluru, to make payments under the Fixed Deposits, as there was no specific reference in the said Will dated 29.10.1997.
The defendants are asserting the rights based on the Will dated 20.06.1983.
The cause of action for the suit arose on the death of B.
Ramalingappa and on subsequent dates of filing the petitions and during the month of May 2006, when the property has been sold by the defendants to the third persons.
Hence, it is prayed to decree the suit.
The plaintiffs were given gold articles worth Rs.1.5 lakhs.
The plaintiffs nor defendant No.4 have raised any objection in respect of the Will of 1983.
The legal representatives of defendant No.3 have made allegations that the defendant No.4's handwriting is seen in the Will dated 29.10.1997.
The plaintiffs also have taken the share of their properties under the Will dated 20.06.1983.
The plaintiffs on one hand claim rights under the Will and wards claim partition under the O.S.No.6422/2006 same Will.
There is no cause of action for filing the suit so also Will is an hindrance of succession.
So, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
The defendant No.5 is the purchaser of the property.
The averments in para No.1 to 8 of the plaint does not pertain to the defendant No.5.
The property has been purchased by defendant No.5 since the properties were in the name of seller and the Will so executed in the year 1997, would not operate against the present defendant No.5.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The health of B. Ramalingappa was so serious and he lost his memory during 1997.
The Will of 1983 was executed in good health and sound mind.
So, the question of executing the Will dated 29.10.1997, does not arise.
The averments made in the Will are such that, it cannot be act upon.
So, the question of considering the Will of 1997, does not arise.
The defendants are contending that, the father had executed a Will in the year 1983, and as per the Will dated 20.06.1983, the shares have been already taken by the children of B. Ramalingappa and they are already in possession and enjoyment of the properties.
So, the question of considering the Will dated 29.10.1997, does not arise.
So, in this regard, the Court has to assess the evidence of the parties.
First and foremost, the plaintiffs have to produce the original Will to prove the Will as well as signature on the Will dated 29.10.1997.
But in this case the plaintiffs did not care to produce the Will dated 29.10.1997 and got marked only a certified copy of the Will dated 29.10.1997.
19.
The plaintiffs have approached the Court seeking their share as per Will dated 29.10.1997.
So, it is the burden on the plaintiffs to produce the original Will and prove the Will as per law by adducing the evidence of attesting witness.
This itself shows that, PW.1 has filed the suit only to make unlawful gain and to harass the defendants.
So, under such circumstances, it is the burden of the plaintiff to prove the Will as per the law laid down, by adducing the evidence of the attesting witness.
So, the suit is filed by the plaintiffs in respect of the second floor open area of the item No.1 of the suit schedule 'A' property.
The right to construct the floors cannot be parted as stated in the Will.
The very bequeath of the property of right to construct in the second floor of item No.1 is impractical and improper.
Whenever there is a Will and rights are put forth by virtue of the O.S.No.6422/2006 Will, the party who comes up with the Will has to produce the Will, and prove in accordance with the law by calling upon the attesting witness to the Court and by identifying the signature of the Testator by the attesting witnesses.
Section 68 of the Evidence Act has to be followed and in this case when the Will has not been proved in accordance with the law, the plaintiff cannot seek any right under the Will of 1997.
41. By the conduct of the parties to the suit, it is clear that the Will of 1983 has already been acted upon.
So, when the plaintiff has come up with a Will to claim the share, certainly the plaintiff ought to have produced the original Will and prove the Will in accordance with the law.
The plaintiffs have failed to prove the Will dated 29.10.1997.
So, under such circumstances, the question of proving the contribution by the defendants does not arise.
So also the question of nonjoinder and misjoinder of necessary parties also does not arise.
The plaintiffs have contended that the father of the plaintiffs has executed a Will of 1997 by cancelling the Will of 1983.
So,
under such circumstances, when the plaintiffs failed to comply the mandatory legal requirement of proving the Will, certainly the plaintiffs cannot seek any share under the Will and certainly there is no cause of action for filing the suit, the Will of 1983 has been already acted upon.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Will of 1983 has been acted upon and all the members of the family are in possession of respective properties as absolute owners.
7. The defendant No.5 being the purchaser of the property, has filed separate written statement and contended that the frame of the suit itself is improper.
opennyai_summary.issue:

O.S.No.6422/2006 ISSUES 1. Whether the plaintiffs prove that the suit schedule properties are the selfacquired properties of their Late father B. Ramalingappa?

5. Whether they further prove that as per the Will dated 20.06.1983, the father of the defendants had separated the suit schedule properties among the plaintiffs and defendants?
6. Whether the defendants No.1 to 3 further prove that the Will dated 20.06.1983 was acted upon?
7. Whether the defendant No.5 proves that the suit is bad for nonjoinder and mis joinder of necessary parties?
8. Whether the defendant No.5 further proves that he purchased the schedule property of the written statement from the defendant No.2 by enquiring the title of defendant No.2?
9. Whether the plaintiffs prove the cause of action?
O.S.No.6422/2006 10. Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to the partition and separate possession of 1/6th share in the suit schedule properties?
What order or decree?
Whether the legal heirs of the defendant No.3 proves that Will dated 29.10.1997 is a concocted,
fabricated and forged document and on the basis of the said document, the plaintiffs are not entitled for the relief?

opennyai_summary.decision:
The plaintiff herein cannot harp upon to the Will dated 29.10.1997.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.9 & 10 in the 'Negative'.
